theme: Regional macro for LatAm and APAC: Mexico INEGI/Banxico, Brazil IBGE/BCB, Argentina INDEC, Colombia DANE, Chile, Japan e-Stat, Korea KOSIS, Australia ABS, India MOSPI clients

candidates.name: sidrapy
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client (MIT, 82 stars, 199 commits, active through at least 2022) for IBGE's SIDRA API. sidrapy.get_table() pulls any SIDRA table by code -- includes tourism/hospitality, PNAD labor, IPCA inflation, industrial production series for Brazil, at whatever frequency/geography IBGE publishes (national, state, municipal). No data committed; it is a live-pull method, so point-in-time care is needed at query time.
candidates.why_useful: Gap #7 (LatAm regional travel volume outside US/EU) -- Brazil is the largest LatAm ABNB market; IBGE SIDRA carries hotel/tourism establishment surveys (PMS - Pesquisa Mensal de Servicos, including hospedagem) and consumer indicators that could proxy Brazil travel demand.
candidates.time_coverage: varies by SIDRA table, many series 1990s-present
candidates.last_activity: active per PyPI (docs at sidrapy.readthedocs.io), commit history through ~2022+

candidates.name: python-bcb
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client (MIT, 127 stars, 22 forks, 235 commits, recent activity/CI visible) for Banco Central do Brasil open-data APIs: SGS time series (many series from 1980s/90s), PTAX daily FX bulletins, and crucially the FOCUS bulletin market-expectations OData endpoint -- Brazil's official weekly consensus survey of analyst forecasts for GDP, inflation, FX, Selic etc. Also real-estate financing (SBPE) and bank-level IFDATA.
candidates.why_useful: Gap #4 (point-in-time historical analyst-consensus snapshots) -- the FOCUS bulletin is a genuine vintage-carrying consensus series (published weekly with as-of dates), a rare real point-in-time macro-expectations dataset, distinct from Bloomberg/FactSet ABNB consensus but useful as a template/comparator and for Brazil-specific FX/GDP nowcasting inputs to the LatAm regional split.
candidates.time_coverage: SGS series from 1980s/90s to present; FOCUS bulletin weekly, several years of history

candidates.name: sie_banxico
candidates.what_it_holds: Small Python wrapper (MIT, 4 stars) for Banco de Mexico's Sistema de Informacion Economica (SIE) API. Documents example series like SF311408/SF311418 (monetary aggregates M1/M2); supports metadata lookup, latest value, historical range queries, percent-change calc, pandas output. Code only, no committed data.
candidates.why_useful: Gap #7 (Mexico regional macro) -- Mexico City is in our Inside Airbnb panel; Banxico SIE carries FX, monetary and (via other series codes) tourism/travel-balance-of-payments indicators (travel receipts) that could feed a Mexico-specific ADR/FX or demand proxy.
candidates.time_coverage: varies by SIE series, many decades of history available via the underlying API

candidates.name: inegiR
candidates.what_it_holds: R package (53 stars, 15 forks) wrapping INEGI's Banco de Indicadores API v2.0. Functions prefixed inind_/incat_ pull GDP, unemployment and other national indicators at annual/quarterly/monthly/biweekly frequency with batch download and catalog/code lookup. Was on CRAN but archived 2026-06-01 for unaddressed issues (note: this is a currently-live compatibility problem per its own README, not a data absence) -- current working version must be installed from GitHub, not CRAN.
candidates.why_useful: Gap #7 (Mexico regional macro) -- broadest indicator coverage of the INEGI candidates found (GDP, employment, and INEGI also publishes hotel-occupancy/tourism series reachable by indicator code through this same API), but flag the CRAN-archive/compatibility caveat before use.
candidates.time_coverage: varies by indicator; INEGI series often 1990s/2000s-present
candidates.license: not fully specified (open source, GitHub-hosted after CRAN archival)
candidates.last_activity: CRAN archived 2026-06-01; GitHub version described as a substantial v3 rewrite for INEGI API compatibility

candidates.name: jpy-datareader
candidates.what_it_holds: Python package (MIT, 26 stars, requires Python >=3.12) providing pandas-DataReader-style remote access to Japan's e-Stat portal: keyword search across statistics tables, metadata retrieval, automatic pagination past 100k rows, filtering by region/time/classification. Covers population/households, labor/wages, agriculture-forestry-fisheries fields explicitly in docs; e-Stat itself also hosts Japan Tourism Statistics / Survey of Overnight Travel Statistics tables reachable the same way. No data committed, code only.
candidates.why_useful: Gap #7 (APAC regional travel volume -- Japan named explicitly). e-Stat is the underlying source for Japan overnight-stay/accommodation survey data (a JNTO-adjacent official series); this client makes it machine-pullable instead of manual portal downloads.

candidates.name: readabs
candidates.what_it_holds: R package (111 stars, 28 forks, 387 commits) that downloads, imports and tidies Australian Bureau of Statistics time series -- both discrete data-cube downloads and the ABS API. Ships convenience wrappers read_cpi(), read_awe() (average weekly earnings), job-mobility, weekly payrolls, and labour-force gross-flows readers; general read_abs_series()/read_abs() cover any ABS catalogue number, which includes ABS Overseas Arrivals and Departures and Tourism Satellite Account tables. Listed in the community 'Awesome Official Statistics Software' list. No data committed.
candidates.why_useful: Gap #7 (APAC -- Australia ABS/TRA named explicitly). ABS publishes Overseas Arrivals & Departures (monthly, by country of origin/purpose of travel) and short-term visitor/departure counts; this is the most mature, actively maintained client found for pulling that series to build an Australia travel-volume proxy.
candidates.time_coverage: most ABS catalogue series run monthly from the 1990s or earlier to present
candidates.license: open source (CRAN/GitHub, see repo for exact license file)
candidates.last_activity: actively maintained per PyPI/CRAN listing and star count

candidates.name: pandaSDMX
candidates.what_it_holds: Python SDMX 2.1 client (Apache 2.0, 134 stars, 928 commits) that queries and parses SDMX-ML/SDMX-JSON from any SDMX-compliant statistical agency (documented providers include World Bank, ILO, BIS, ECB, Eurostat, OECD, UNICEF, UN) and returns pandas objects. Several LatAm/APAC national statistical offices (e.g. DANE Colombia, some ABS Australia collections, and OECD's country tourism tables which include Mexico, Chile, Korea, Japan, Australia, India as OECD/G20 members) expose SDMX endpoints reachable through this same client, though not all are pre-registered as named 'agencies' in the library -- would need per-agency endpoint config.
candidates.why_useful: General-purpose acquisition method spanning several numbered-gap countries (7) at once via OECD's SDMX tourism/consumer tables (which include non-EU OECD members: Mexico, Chile, Colombia, Korea, Japan, Australia) rather than one country-specific client each.
candidates.geography: multi-country (SDMX-compliant agencies, incl. OECD members: Mexico, Chile, Colombia, Korea, Japan, Australia)
candidates.last_activity: 928 commits, docs at pandasdmx.readthedocs.io, appears actively maintained

notes: MAJOR CONSTRAINT: this session's WebSearch tool returned 'budget exhausted (200 of 200)' on the very first query, before this scout ran any searches itself -- the 200-query session budget is evidently shared across all concurrent scout subagents in this sweep, and scout #101 got essentially none of it. Fell back to WebFetch on github.com/search (which then hit GitHub's own 429 rate limit, likely for the same reason -- shared IP/session across scouts) and then to WebFetch on PyPI/CRAN package pages (which don't count against WebSearch budget and were not rate-limited) to identify GitHub repo URLs via package metadata, followed by direct WebFetch verification of each candidate repo. This means coverage here is biased toward countries with well-known, guessable PyPI/CRAN package names (Brazil, Mexico, Japan, Australia via SDMX-adjacent tooling) and is much weaker for Korea (KOSIS), Colombia (DANE), Chile (Banco Central), Argentina (INDEC/Datos Argentina series-tiempo-ar), and India (MOSPI) -- for these five, guessed package/repo names returned dead pages or 404s and no verified candidate could be produced. If another pass has WebSearch budget available, prioritize: 'KOSIS API client site:github.com', 'DANE Colombia API python github', 'Banco Central Chile API python github', 'series de tiempo AR github python' (Argentina's official Datos Argentina API has a documented Python client, likely at github.com/datosgobar), and 'MOSPI India NSS data github' / 'data.gov.in API python client github'. None of the fully verified finds directly hold a committed dataset -- all seven are acquisition methods (live API clients), consistent with CONTEXT.md's framing that tooling counts. No committed CSVs, no release-asset dumps, and no pointer-to-Zenodo/Kaggle/Dataverse candidates were found for this theme in the time available.
